newsitem.title: UK: YEAREND-S.African stocks set to improve in '97.
newsitem.headline: YEAREND-S.African stocks set to improve in '97.

text.p: South African shares may be flat early in 1997, weighed down by a sluggish economy, but fair earnings growth and improving confidence should lift prices in the second half, a Reuters survey showed.

A poll of 11 equity strategists, conducted towards the close of a choppy year on the South African bourse, found stocks were expected to appreciate more than 15 percent in 1997 after a meagre seven percent this year.
Following are a selection of views on next year's performance of the Johannesbburg stock exchange:
DAVID SHAPIRO, JOINT MANAGING DIRECTOR SOCIETE GENERALE FRANKEL POLLAK
"It's going to be a slow start but by year-end things should start to kick up here -- that's based on world economies.
"If we're not (around the 8,200 level) by the end of the year, then we're in trouble. Then it means that none of South Africa's economic plans are working."

"The market might be a bit nervous in the second half of 1998 ahead of the (general election) in April 1999. There might be a bit of a slowdown as the market discounts the succession (to President Nelson Mandela) and possible violence."
DENZIL NEWMAN, PORTFOLIO MANAGER SYFRETS MANAGED ASSETS
"We see 1997 earnings growth up by 15 to 20 percent but I would expect something of a derating so we would put this market up only between 10 and 15 percent next year."
